author: North Raleigh Today
title: Amazon Music offers various plans for Prime members and non-members
text:
Andy Jassy | President and CEO of Amazon.com | Amazon website
Andy Jassy | President and CEO of Amazon.com | Amazon website
Amazon Music offers a variety of plans to cater to different user needs, including Prime members and non-members. Prime members enjoy Amazon Music as part of their membership benefits, which includes access to over 100 million tracks in shuffle mode and ad-free top podcasts at no extra cost. Additionally, they have access to curated playlists, artist livestreams, in-app merchandise, and exclusive podcasts.
For those not subscribed to Prime, Amazon Music Unlimited is available for $11.99 per month or $10.99 per month for Prime members. This plan provides on-demand access to Amazon's full catalog of over 100 million songs and podcasts without ads. It also includes Audible’s selection of audiobooks for users in the U.S., UK, and Canada with one audiobook per month.
There is also a free version of Amazon Music that allows access to over 100 million ad-supported tracks. Users can select songs within All-Access Playlists but will experience ads outside these playlists.
Amazon offers various service tiers so users can choose based on their preferences and budget. The family plan costs $10.99 per month or $109 annually, allowing up to six family members to listen simultaneously on different devices.
